barriers.reason: Cardiac rehab requires rides three mornings a week for 12 weeks, but the patient does not drive, has no license, Harold previously drove, and the patient arrived today by cab with no standing ride arrangement.
Rehab appointments conflict with the patient's sole responsibility for Harold, who cannot be left alone; the neighbor who watches him is available only two hours and the patient already owes her.

alternatives.text: Ask the cardiac rehab program for chair/class times on days that match an available ride or when someone can stay with Harold.

If a disability or health condition prevents using fixed-route buses/trains, apply for ADA Paratransit certification (Northern Illinois Transit Authority, 312-663-HELP); note certification takes time and rides run only when fixed-route service runs.

Check the patient's coverage for non-emergency medical transportation: Medicaid/dual members can use MCO NEMT (call the number on the plan card) or Transdev for fee-for-service; Medicare-only patients generally do not have a covered routine ride benefit unless their Medicare Advantage plan includes one.
